To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

biochar induced negative priming of native SOC in the presence but not in the absence of plants and that biochar C is highly stable with a MRT between 350 and 500 years in a rhodic ferralosol under subtropical conditions.
Biochar addition to an annual ryegruss pasture system resulted in a significant reduction in SOC mineralisation and a significant increase in root derived respiration.
the presence of an active C 3 plant community in a C 4 dominant soil system reduced SOC mineralisation in response to biochar application.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the priming of soil and biochar C, the C 4 to C 3 plant shift and the impact of plants on the longevity of biochar C under field conditions.
the priming effect of biochar in the field and the C sequestration potential of biochar.
the priming effects of biochar on the mineralisation of soil and root derived C and its longevity under field conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
biochar C longevity is greater than the current mean residence time of SOC (i.e. 1000 years).
the biochar induced negative priming of the SOC pool was driven by the interaction between plant and biochar, and was transient in nature.
biochar induced negative priming was observed under field conditions in a subtropical ferralsol, with no net priming in unplanted soils.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of plants in this subtropical soil did not affect biochar C stability and that biochar induced negative priming of native SOC in this system.
biochar induced negative priming of native SOC in the presence or absence of growing plants, and the presence/absence plants had no impact of biochar C mineralization in this ferralsoil.
biochar C is a long term stable C pool in subtropical soil systems, but its effect on SOC mineralisation in the presence of plants is transient and dependent on the experimental timeframe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
biochar C is stable and does not contribute to the transient SOC pools under field conditions in subtropical Australia.
biochar can have a positive impact on soil C stocks by reducing the mineralisation of SOC.
biochar C longevity is not impacted by the presence of plants in a subtropical soil, and that biochar can induce a negative priming effect of soil organic matter under field conditions.
